title: The FRANK Standard — Dubai Leasing & Property Management
disclaimer: Educational draft, not legal advice or accredited training. Verify tenancy terms and current regulations through DLD/RERA and qualified advisers.

chapters.title: Landlord Instructions, Leasing Authority and Property Readiness
outcomes: Establish clear rental mandate and service scope
sections: Who can instruct the lease

A property manager, family member or broker may be communicating with you without being the owner. Confirm current ownership and lawful authority to instruct leasing and sign tenancy documents. Record the legal landlord and the permitted representative. A marketing instruction does not itself resolve power-of-attorney or tenancy-signing authority.
Readiness checklist

Inspect property condition, utilities, appliances, safety-related issues, photographs, accessibility, keys and any relevant building or community restrictions. Distinguish promised repairs from completed work. The property's condition should be recorded before inviting deposits or promising occupancy.
Commercial mandate

Record target rent, negotiable terms, payment frequency, deposit, listing authority, commission, furnishing inclusions, lease length, maintenance policy and whether the property is available immediately. If the landlord wants to discriminate unlawfully against a group or asks you to invent occupancy rules, escalate rather than applying an unsupported restriction.
Evidence, not optimism

Show achievable rent using comparable registered tenancies where available, competing listings and current vacancy. Differentiate asking price from achieved rent, and explicitly factor payment structure, furnishing and maintenance. A high advertised rent with months of vacancy may yield a weaker result than a realistic rent and fast occupancy.

quiz.q: Who can authorize you to lease the unit?
options: The owner or an appropriately authorized representative
A tenant who knows the building
quiz.why: Authority must be established before acting for the landlord.

chapters.title: Tenant Qualification, Offers and Fair Practice
outcomes: Explain the full rent and fee commitment
sections: Objective tenant screening

Assess the proposed occupancy, affordable cash commitments, payment schedule, contract duration, and information necessary for the transaction. Use a consistent documented policy and respect applicable privacy and anti-discrimination obligations. Avoid inventing eligibility requirements or collecting information that has no legitimate purpose.
True cost of moving

Explain upfront rent installments, security deposit, commissions if applicable, utility activation and registration costs. A renter may be able to cover monthly equivalent rent but not a large initial cheque; make the payment timing clear before taking a holding amount.
Offer handling

Create a written offer summary specifying unit, rent, number and timing of payments, security deposit, start date, furnishing, repairs, included utilities, pet or occupancy conditions where lawful, and any material terms. Distinguish a landlord-approved offer from a binding signed tenancy contract.
Deposit and receipts

Do not imply a reservation payment is automatically refundable or nonrefundable. Explain the written purpose, authorized payee and circumstances for return or application, and issue proper documentation. Keep the tenant informed if another offer is accepted; avoid artificial competition.

quiz.q: A tenant can afford the monthly rent but not four months upfront. What should the agent discuss?
options: Different payment frequency or a suitable alternative, with landlord consent
Promise the landlord will accept later
quiz.why: Payment timing and tenant affordability are both part of suitability.

chapters.title: Tenancy Terms, Ejari and Registration Pathways
outcomes: Avoid reliance on outdated Ejari fees or workflows
sections: What Ejari records

Ejari is the official Dubai tenancy contract registration framework. It is not a substitute for agreeing all obligations in the tenancy agreement. The lease should clearly identify parties, property, term, rent/payment dates, security deposit, maintenance obligations, occupancy and notices. Current official registration instructions should be consulted for each relevant channel.
Channel eligibility

DLD lists trustee centers and digital channels, with different procedures depending on the applicant, owner and management arrangement. Some actions require owner approval or authorized representative documentation. Never tell a tenant that a specific remote workflow is available without checking the current account and eligibility conditions.
Fees must be verified

The official DLD service page lists registration and service partner charges, and those may differ by digital versus in-person channel. Show the date checked and link directly rather than permanently baking an amount into a training slide that could age. Clarify who pays pursuant to the agreement and applicable requirements.
Document completion

Ensure the final tenancy terms match the registration inputs and any owner authorization. Save the correct registration certificate, contract version and receipts in the authorized transaction file. Escalate mismatches or rejected registrations instead of reusing a prior tenant's documents.

quiz.q: What is the safe source for a current Ejari fee?
options: DLD's current service channel and fees page
quiz.why: Fees and eligibility depend on current official instructions and channel.

chapters.title: Handover, Maintenance, Rent Collection and Service Quality
outcomes: Prevent avoidable disputes over deposits and defects
sections: The handover record

Create a signed inventory and condition checklist with dated photographs where permitted, meter readings, issued keys, access cards, remotes and appliance condition. Note defects awaiting resolution and assigned deadlines. If a handover is rushed, document unresolved issues rather than issuing a misleading clean checklist.
Maintenance clarity

Differentiate landlord responsibilities, tenant responsibilities, routine servicing, emergency repairs and alterations as provided in the applicable agreement and law. Explain escalation contacts and response expectations. Do not promise that all maintenance is free or automatically charge every defect to the tenant.
Collection workflow

Maintain a clear rent schedule, payments received, receipts issued, arrears follow-up and communication record, with privacy and money-handling controls. Make reminders factual. A late payment is not permission to lock out a tenant, remove utilities or apply arbitrary penalties.
Service recovery

When a defect or payment dispute arises, record the facts, inspect the relevant documents and refer unresolved legal matters to qualified professionals or authorities. Good property management uses predictable documented service processes; it avoids threats, assumptions and disappearing after the lease is signed.

quiz.q: Which is the strongest safeguard against a later deposit-condition dispute?
options: Dated inventory, photographic evidence where permitted, and signed handover
quiz.why: Documenting the initial condition makes later differences more objectively assessable.

chapters.title: Renewals, Rent Changes, Notices and Dispute Prevention
outcomes: Differentiate official rent guidance from landlord preference
Recognize when legal advice or dispute resolution is necessary
sections: Renewal timeline

Track expiry, permitted notice periods, landlord and tenant communications, proposed financial changes and registration requirements. Do not invent a blanket number of days from an old blog; identify the current statutory framework and the actual contract terms. Have a documented renewal calendar for each property.
Rent increase analysis

Use the appropriate current official mechanism and rules for rent changes rather than a generic percentage or inflation assumption. Separate landlord target rent from a legally supportable proposal. Explain what is known, what needs official verification and what requires professional review.
Dispute escalation

Treat disagreements on renewal, repairs, eviction, deductions or access as legal-risk events. Preserve notices, repair requests, receipts and the signed contract. Do not coach unlawful self-help remedies or promise eviction outcomes. Identify the appropriate authority or qualified lawyer when the issue cannot be resolved commercially.
Investment view of retention

A renewal is not just administrative: compare realistic alternative rental income against vacancy loss, agent commission, refurbishment expenses, tenant quality and collection reliability. For example, a AED 5,000 annual rental increase may be economically unattractive if the property remains vacant for two months. Present a net comparison, not just a new advertised rent.

quiz.q: Can a landlord automatically impose any rent increase they want?
options: No; verify the applicable current rules and valid process
Yes, provided the tenant is contacted by WhatsApp
quiz.why: Renewal changes must follow applicable law, contract and official processes.
